description: Central strategy capacity is strong but revision authority and community feedback are limited.
Local resilience offices combine technical feedback with lived community information.
Asset monitoring is stronger than public feedback or authority for structural change.
Global systems gather information but struggle with enforcement and revision authority.
Regulators can evaluate evidence but may lack speed and public participation.
Preparedness agencies need strong surveillance plus lasting institutional memory.
Civic assemblies surface legitimacy and justice signals often missed by formal institutions.
Digital modernization offices detect usage signals but may miss rights and legitimacy concerns.
